decisions.reason: As a core upholstery fabric very close to the firm's established capabilities, it fits existing design and development knowledge well and is more likely to be refined than withdrawn.
This decorative fabric remains close enough to the firm's core range for market feedback to be absorbed and used, though its lower prominence keeps some pruning risk.
The flame-retardant jacquard curtain fabric matches the firm's contract-textile and functional know-how especially well, making retention and incremental improvement the most likely path.
The product builds on familiar decorative textile competences, but as a more niche wool-blend item it still carries a moderate rationalisation risk if demand or sustainability fit disappoints.

The firm has enough related knowledge to keep learning and adjust this technically adjacent fabric, yet its niche positioning and material complexity make it the most vulnerable among the older launches.
As a 2024 launch with dedicated visibility and strong overlap with the firm's upholstery and curtain expertise, it is likely to be given time and development effort rather than removed quickly.
